titulo: Ci and ne: Ne: quantity and topic

aula.objetivo: Use «ci» for a place already named and for an idea, use «ne» for quantity and topic, and put both pronouns in the right place. Avoid the English-speaker traps: dropping the pronoun, leaving it after the verb, and leaving out «ne» when the noun is gone.

itens.pt: to think of it (to have an opinion)

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «ne» means «of it» or «of them». It replaces «di» + a noun, and it is mostly used for quantities. STEP 2: quantity: «Hai mangiato due mele? Sì, ne ho mangiate due» (I ate two of them). The noun disappears, but the number stays. In English you can drop the noun: «I ate two». In Italian you cannot drop it without «ne». STEP 3: «un po' di» also needs «ne»: «Vuoi del caffè? Sì, ne voglio un po'» (I want a little). STEP 4: in the passato prossimo, the participle agrees with the thing counted: «Ne ho mangiate due» (le mele), «Ne ho comprati tre» (i libri). STEP 5: topic: «di» + a subject: «parlare di» → «parlarne» (to talk about it), «pensare di» → «pensarne» (to have an opinion of it): «Che ne pensi?» means «What do you think of it?». STEP 6: «pensarci» and «pensarne» are different. «Ci penso» means «I am thinking about it» (it is on my mind), and «Che ne pensi?» asks for an opinion. STEP 7: «averne abbastanza» means «to have had enough»: «Ne ho abbastanza». STEP 8: «ne» goes in the same place as other pronouns: before the verb, after «non», and attached to the infinitive.
blocos.comparacao: English leaves the noun out when the quantity is clear: «I ate two», «I want a little», «How many do you have? Three». Italian does not allow the bare number after a verb: you must say «Ne ho mangiate due», «Ne voglio un po'», «Quanti ne hai? Ne ho tre». If you hear a small «ne» in a sentence with a number, it stands for the missing noun. For opinions, English uses «think of» and «think about» almost interchangeably. Italian separates the two ideas: «pensarci» (to have something on your mind) and «pensarne» (to have an opinion).

exemplos.pt: What do you think of it

erros.motivo: The noun is gone, so you need «ne» to carry it, and the participle then agrees with the thing counted: «ne ho mangiate due».
Without the noun, «un po'» needs «ne»: «ne voglio un po'».
